newsitem.title: UK: HK stocks in London fall, Merrill lowers weighting.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks in London fall, Merrill lowers weighting.

text.p: Hong Kong shares trading in London eased across the board on Wednesday, with sentiment dampened by news that Merrill Lynch expected a Hang Seng correction and was reducing its weighting in Hong Kong.

"We've seen prices lower across the board, they've been brought back by the news about Merrill Lynch cutting their weighting," one dealer said. "There has been some selling of utilities, otherwise it's been mostly markdowns."
By 1408 GMT the Hang Seng London reference index was 84.8 points or 0.59 percent lower at 14,337.04.
The Hang Seng closed 18.19 points lower in Hong Kong on Wednesday after a day of hefty price swings.
Merrill Lynch said it expected a 10-15 percent Hang Seng correction in the next few months. Research director Adrian Faure said 13,000 points was fair value for the index.
Merrill said it would increase its weighting in South Korea and the Philippines at the expense of Hong Kong. -- Andrew Marshall, London newsroom +44 171 542 4026
